THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

These appeals are filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) calling in question the judgment and award dated 07.02.2018, passed in M.V.C.No.4778/2016, on the file of the IIIrd Additional Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, at Bengaluru (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity).
MFA No.6482/2018 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.
MFA No.5518/2018 is filed by the insurance company praying to reduce the quantum of compensation.
Brief facts:
2.

sentences.text: On 19.06.2016, at about 9.00 a.m., the claimant was riding his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-S-6329 from Hegganahalli towards Sunkadakatte on Hegganahalli Main Road, at that time the rider of the Motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-HZ-2729 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the claimant.
As a result, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant- claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part,
and awarded a compensation of Rs.3,86,792/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondents therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
1. Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 40,000/-
2. Loss of Amenities in Life : Rs. 10,000/-

As per the Wound Certificate at Exhibit-P5, Discharge Summary at Exhibit-P12, coupled with the evidence of PW-2, Doctor and the documentary evidence, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries:
"i) Lacerated wound measuring 2.5 cms. x 1 cm x 0.5 cms over the anterior aspect of distal end of right leg;
ii) Swelling, restricted movements and deformity over the lower end of right leg."
7.
The aforesaid injuries are grievous in nature.
The claimant was aged 40 years old.
Considering this, the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Pain and Sufferings, at Rs.40,000/-, is on lesser side and hence the sum is enhanced to Rs.60,000/- is awarded.
8. The Doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant had suffered 57% physical disability towards right lower limb and 19% physical disability to the whole-body.
The Tribunal has considered the physical disability @ 12% to the particular limb and 10% disability to the whole- body.
The criteria for calculating functional disability is elaborately discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another1 (2011) 1 SCC 343

considering the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court stated supra, and the injuries suffered by the appellant and the avocation of the appellant-claimant; the appellant was in the business in Services Proprietor of Vajragiri Management Services, A.T. Road, Sanjeevini Nagar,
Heganahalli, Bengaluru; the said nature of job requires field work.
Hence, the assessment of disability made by the Tribunal at 12% as functional disability to the whole-body is found to be correct.
The other para-meters are found be correct.
Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under 'Loss of future Income Due to Disability' at Rs.2,16,000/- is appropriate and the same is kept in tact.
